instruction:
Fix `packages/frontend-app-api/src/wiring/phaseApis.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. major (line 442): collectDeferredRouteInstances calls instantiateAppNodeSubtree on each route-bearing node with no skipChild. That runs the factory of every descendant during bootstrap, including non-route content such as entity cards under an entity page. visitDeferred then recurses and instantiates every nested route-bearing descendant (sub-pages, EntityContent) again from scratch, so a node at depth d with route-bearing ancestors runs its factory up to d+1 times before finalization. This contradicts the plan's U03 rule 5 intent ('nodes without such outputs are never instantiated ... other content factories do not run during bootstrap') and adds startup cost that grows with the app's size. Confidence: high on the behaviour, medium on how much it matters in real apps. — fix: Instantiate each route-bearing node on its own (for example, skipChild: () => true) and fall back to the full detached subtree only when that produces no instance, for example when a required input is missing. Or instantiate only the top-most route-bearing node and reuse its detached descendants, not re-instantiating them.
2. minor (line 379): The wrapper uses two 'as unknown as' casts: one to call cached.func with unknown[] args and one to cast the arrow function to RouteFunc<TParams>. This erases the parameter typing of RouteFunc inside the proxy. It was introduced in the tsc fix round. — fix: Type the wrapper as '(...args: Parameters<RouteFunc<TParams>>) => cached.func(...args)' with a single cast to RouteFunc<TParams> if needed, or add a one-line comment explaining why the double cast is required.
3. minor (line 376): After finalization, if the finalized resolver can no longer resolve the ref (for example, the page was disabled by a predicate), the wrapper silently falls back to the bootstrap function and keeps producing a link to a route that no longer exists. The plan specifies this behaviour, but it is not documented in the code. — fix: Add a short why-comment at the fallback stating that this is intentional, or return the stale path only while the delegate is unchanged. Leave the behaviour as the plan specifies it.
